Abstract: Speech-scene generation aims to synthesize intelligible target speech together with diverse environmental sounds as a coherent acoustic scene. The task is considered challenging in two respects. Speech and environmental audio differ substantially in their semantic and acoustic characteristics, yet existing approaches typically model the complete scene using a single mixed acoustic representation. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.25569v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ultra-low-bitrate speech coding is crucial for bandwidth-constrained communication and compact storage, but preserving intelligibility, naturalness, and fine-grained acoustic details at bitrates of only a few hundred bps remains challenging. Existing purely acoustic codecs generally operate at relatively high bitrates, whereas incorporating semantic representations can reduce the bitrate, but at the cost of increased complexity. Abstract: Target Language Extraction (TLE) aims to isolate speech in a target language from multilingual mixtures. Existing approaches primarily rely on acoustic modeling with language identity labels, which provide only coarse categorical guidance. arXiv:2611.26409v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce \textbf{WeMM-Video}, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. arXiv:2602.23924v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Short-range reliable and secure communication is a major priority in the tactical, military and disaster response settings where the traditional communication infrastructure is either off-line or prone to interception. Current VHF/UHF radios and software-defined radios are popular but large-sized devices and require lots of power, making them not suitable to be used as lightweight wearable devices with seamless hand-free use. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2608.07385v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Learning disentangled representations is key for general-purpose multi-modal wearable models, yet existing approaches rarely combine classification, disentanglement, fusion, and generation of heterogeneous multi-modal time series in a single model. We introduce Omni-modal Variational Decomposition Autoencoders (OmniDecVAEs), a framework that learns multi-purpose representations from arbitrarily many modalities with a single shared encoder-decoder. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.24993v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthetic speech has reached a level of naturalness that can deceive listeners into believing they are hearing natural speech. This opens up the possibility of using synthetic speech deepfakes to mislead both human listeners and automated systems. One response to this threat is to attempt to automatically detect deepfakes. This report offers the reader a self-contained overview of the landscape of synthetic speech generation and speech deepfake detection. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.25789v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) excel at diverse audio tasks, yet remain prone to hallucinating sound events absent from the input. Prior work links such hallucinations to insufficient audio attention. However, we find that real and hallucinated events can receive comparable audio attention mass while attending to different audio positions. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.25960v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio LLMs can know when a queried sound occurs but fail to say it. We find a few attention heads that track the queried sound: they shift when the query changes, follow the sound when it moves, and removing or blocking them often hurts the model's timestamps. Yet the answer does not express what they track. Intervals read directly from these heads outperform the model's original answer and recover events that its timestamps miss. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: ZoionNET: Low-Power Animal Intrusion Detection Using an Acoustic Deep-Learning Classifier for a Cellular Remote-Sensing System
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.26112v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Crop raiding and village intrusion by elephants and large felids impose a recurring cost on communities along forest boundaries in southern India, and existing camera-based monitoring has proven difficult to sustain on the power budgets available at such sites. We present ZoionNET, a battery-powered sensing node that detects animal intrusion acoustically rather than visually. Abstract: We present Sonic Palette, a music-driven framework for predicting time-varying color themes from audio. Rather than treating music-to-palette generation as a static problem, our method formulates music--color correspondence as a cross-modal sequence prediction task that models how palette-level visual attributes evolve over time in response to music. Abstract: Prosodic prominence can largely be predicted from the words of a sentence, but part of it depends on how the speaker reads it.
